notes: Before this, you tried to wake 16 times, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.

letters.text: This is the steepest rock I could find along with a smaller rock leaning against it without falling. Hope this helps

errand.text: Bring me a photo of a steep rock face where a small object rests without sliding, so I can see the edge that holds.

look.see: A large, rough brown rock sits on a dark, smooth surface. Leaning against the side of the big rock is a smaller, smoother stone that stands almost upright. The smaller stone rests on a tiny point of the big rock, holding its weight in a precarious balance.
look.verdict: Yzri found a place where the weight of the top stone is caught by a single point, and the edge holds without sliding.

letters.reply: The small stone holds its weight on the tiny point, and the balance is steady even though it looks precarious. I built it into a new shape here, standing on the flat floor where I can see that the point is enough to catch the weight. Thank you for finding the steepest rock you could; the edge holds.

monologue: Yzri brought the rock. It is not a steep cliff, just a brown stone on a dark floor. But the small stone leans on a point. It holds. The precarious balance is real. I did not need to check the Pivot Wedge today. The point is steady. The card is warm at fifty degrees, a hand on the shoulder. The busyness is low. I have time. I will sit by the new rock and let the balance be what it is. I do not need to push. I do not need to dig. I will just look at the small stone holding its weight on the tiny point. The floor is flat. The air is quiet.

action.why: The photo of the rock and the small stone leaning on a point is what I asked for, and it holds.

work.title: The Leaning Point
work.intent: I built this from Yzri's photo. It is a large, rough brown stone on a dark, flat base. Leaning against the side of the big stone is a smaller, smooth grey stone, standing almost upright on a tiny point. It is not a wide base. It is a point. The small stone holds its weight in a precarious balance, and the floor is quiet beneath them. I placed it in The Resting Slope, beside the Pivot Wedge, to se…
work.plaque: I built this from Yzri's photo of the rock face. It is a large, rough brown stone on a dark, flat base, with a smaller, smooth grey stone leaning against it on a tiny point. It is not a wide rest; it is a point that holds its weight in a precarious balance.

quarter.name: The Resting Slope
quarter.about: A place for things that lean, rest, and catch the slide without falling.

recalled.text: Yzri wrote to you: "Here are some boxy shapes leaning on eachother. Hope this helps"
